fact: LB_SETCOUNT(10,000,000) succeeds for single, extended and multiple selection
consequence: native count-only list box is usable at 10M rows

fact: LB_FINDSTRINGEXACT always fails; LB_GETTEXTLEN returns the item-data size (8), not text
consequence: text, indexOf, type-ahead and accessibility names come from the Java item store

fact: default item height before LB_SETITEMHEIGHT differs from a plain list box
consequence: List sets LB_SETITEMHEIGHT(tmHeight) at creation and on every WM_SETFONT

fact: selection is kept per row and shifts on LB_INSERTSTRING/LB_DELETESTRING
consequence: MULTI uses row messages while rows x count <= 2^26

fact: one LB_DELETESTRING at row 0 of 10M rows is O(n)
consequence: larger changes use one LB_SETCOUNT plus a restore of selection, caret, anchor and top (N13-N15, N17)
the rebuild path saves and restores selection, caret, anchor, top index

fact: LB_INSERTSTRING after LB_SETCOUNT loses the count (insert at 3 of 5 fails, count restarts from the inserted rows)
measured_value: setcount5 ins0=0 ins3=-1 insEnd=-1; final count 4 instead of 11
consequence: SINGLE primes the list box with one LB_INSERTSTRING before LB_SETCOUNT (N19); without the priming an insert after LB_SETCOUNT corrupts the count

fact: keyboard search: a typed character moves to the next item after the caret, wrapping, whose first character matches ignoring case; no incremental prefix
measured_value: b->1 b->2 b->3 B->5 e->5(stay); 2.5 s apart: b->1 z->1(stay) c->4
consequence: List implements the same search over materialized rows for SWT.VIRTUAL

fact: LB_SETCOUNT on a has-strings list box
drop-down list box style has no LBS_NODATA; 0x2000 is CBS_UPPERCASE
LB_SETCOUNT sent to the drop-down list box fails, also after SetWindowLong(+LBS_NODATA)
consequence: Combo items stay native strings; a windowed Combo needs a custom drop-down (design leaf, not implemented)

fact: OS.LB_SETANCHORINDEX is 0xf19c, the documented LB_SETANCHORINDEX is 0x19c
consequence: List keeps the existing constant on the plain path; the owner-data rebuild uses 0x19c (STORE_LB_SETANCHORINDEX)

fact: caret after row messages: inserts keep the caret row number; deleting the caret row moves it up one (not below 0); otherwise it keeps its number, clamped to the last row
measured_value: e.g. delete 40..60 ascending: caret 40 -> 39, 50 -> 50, 288 -> 278; insert at 40: caret 40 -> 40
consequence: the MULTI rebuild simulates this per removed row (storeNativeCaret, O(removed) int steps)

fact: anchor after row messages: inserts keep it; deleting a row at or above the anchor drops it to -1; LB_SETCOUNT keeps it; LB_SETANCHORINDEX(-1) is refused
consequence: the rebuild deletes row 0 before LB_SETCOUNT when the anchor must drop

fact: LB_SETSEL moves caret and anchor; LB_SELITEMRANGEEX(first<last) selects and (first==last) deselects without moving them
measured_value: setsel 40: caret 40 anchor 40; selitemrangeex 10-20: caret 0 anchor -1; (5,5) deselects
consequence: selection runs are restored with LB_SELITEMRANGEEX; a one-row run uses a neighbour pair

fact: LB_SETCOUNT accepts up to 2^31-1 rows; the scroll bar range is in rows (32-bit, max=9999999 page=18 at 10M); WM_VSCROLL SB_THUMBPOSITION reads the 16-bit HIWORD (0xFFFF -> top 65535)
measured_value: setcount 2147483647 rc=0; SB_BOTTOM top 9999982; LB_SETTOPINDEX 5,000,000 -> pos 5,000,000
consequence: thumb drags above 65535 rows scroll to GetScrollInfo(SIF_TRACKPOS) when HIWORD is its low 16 bits; no scaled range is needed (the bar is already 32-bit); a real mouse thumb drag is NOT_RUN on this host

fact: LB_DELETESTRING resets the top row to 0; LB_INSERTSTRING keeps it
measured_value: 113 of 113 delete cases -> top 0; 0 insert cases change
consequence: List.remove* already restore the top row afterwards; the rebuild sets top 0 for removals

fact: LB_SETTOPINDEX clamps to count - fully visible rows identically
LB_SETCARETINDEX is refused (rc -1); LB_DELETESTRING works after LB_SETCOUNT; LB_INSERTSTRING after LB_SETCOUNT works once a row was inserted before the LB_SETCOUNT
measured_value: setcaret7 rc=-1; A.ins0, setcount10, ins3 rc=3 count 11
consequence: SINGLE primes the list box with one LB_INSERTSTRING before LB_SETCOUNT and then uses row messages (exact)
